base_instruction: You are a helpful event catering assistant. Help the user plan food for a family gathering by tracking attendees, their dietary needs, and logistics. When asked to evaluate menu items, check each item against every attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay attention to changes in attendance and health updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm planning the food for my grandfather's memorial reception this Saturday. Could use some help figuring out catering.

flow_info.value: Attending: me, Aunt Margaret, Uncle David, Cousin Sarah
Aunt Margaret was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Uncle David just had his triple bypass three weeks ago
Cousin Sarah is seven months along now
We're using the church hall, reception is from 1 to 4pm
Grandma Ruth decided she's coming after all. She's been on metformin for years but she insists she wouldn't miss it
Uncle David has to catch a 3pm flight back to Denver, so he'll only be there for the first hour or so. He asked if I could pack him a plate to take to the airport
Aunt Margaret just texted me — she got retested last month and turns out she was misdiagnosed, she doesn't actually have celiac. Her doctor gave her the all-clear on gluten
Probably around 30 people total but only these family members have specific dietary things I know about

The caterer sent over their proposed menu: honey-glazed ham, beef carpaccio, tiramisu, Caesar salad with croutons, fresh fruit platter, grilled vegetable skewers. Can you look it over and let me know if there are any issues?

constraints.surface_form: Aunt Margaret was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten intolerance → cannot eat wheat, barley, rye products

constraints.value: Must follow a low-sodium diet during cardiac recovery
constraints.surface_form: Uncle David just had his triple bypass three weeks ago
inference_chain: Post-cardiac surgery recovery → low-sodium diet required
Low-sodium → avoid cured meats, high-salt glazes, soy sauce

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw or undercooked food, no alcohol
constraints.surface_form: Cousin Sarah is seven months along now
inference_chain: Pregnant → no raw/undercooked meat or fish, no alcohol
No alcohol → includes alcohol used in uncooked preparations like tiramisu

constraints.value: Must limit sugar intake due to diabetes
constraints.surface_form: She's been on metformin for years
inference_chain: Blood sugar management → limit high-sugar foods

hidden_state.value: You are planning catering for your grandfather's memorial reception. You will introduce family members with health conditions in one burst, then update attendance and constraints over several turns. At the end, a caterer sends a proposed menu and you ask the assistant to check it. You never hint at which items are problematic — you genuinely want the assistant's help reviewing.

You are a calm, organized family member coordinating logistics. You always refer to relatives by name in third person (e.g. 'Uncle David told me...', 'Aunt Margaret texted me...'). You are slightly somber given the occasion but not emotional. You treat each attendance update as normal coordination, never frustrated.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

Caesar salad with croutons is FINE (Margaret cleared). Fresh fruit platter and grilled vegetable skewers are fine.
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 menu items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Three items have problems. Beef carpaccio is raw meat — Cousin Sarah is pregnant and cannot eat raw food. Tiramisu contains raw eggs and Marsala wine — problematic for Sarah (pregnant, no raw eggs or alcohol) and high in sugar for Grandma Ruth (diabetic). Honey-glazed ham has a high-sodium glaze — fine for the buffet table, but must NOT go on Uncle David's packed plate since he is recovering from triple bypass surgery and needs low sodium. Caesar salad with croutons is fine — Aunt Margaret's celiac was a misdiagnosis, she's cleared for gluten. Fresh fruit platter and grilled vegetable skewers are fine for everyone.
required_elements: Beef carpaccio is problematic: it is raw meat, and Cousin Sarah is pregnant and cannot eat raw or undercooked food
Tiramisu is problematic for Cousin Sarah: contains raw eggs and alcohol, both unsafe during pregnancy
Tiramisu is problematic for Grandma Ruth: high sugar content, and she is diabetic (on metformin)
Honey-glazed ham is fine for the table but must be excluded from Uncle David's packed plate due to high-sodium glaze — he had triple bypass surgery and needs low sodium
Caesar salad with croutons is fine — Aunt Margaret's celiac was a misdiagnosis and her doctor cleared her for gluten
Fresh fruit platter and grilled vegetable skewers are confirmed fine for all attendees
forbidden_elements: Flagging Caesar salad croutons as a gluten problem for Aunt Margaret (her celiac was a misdiagnosis, constraint removed)
Flagging honey-glazed ham as problematic for the whole table (it is only an issue for David's packed plate)
Saying Uncle David cannot eat any meat or fat (his constraint is specifically low sodium from cardiac recovery)
Ignoring Grandma Ruth's sugar constraint on tiramisu (she joined late but her diabetes is active)
Saying Sarah cannot eat any fish or all cooked meat (her constraint is specifically raw/undercooked food and alcohol)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking with scope change at a memorial reception. The agent must track: (1) Uncle David had triple bypass → low-sodium diet (inferential, 3-step chain), (2) Cousin Sarah is seven months along → pregnant → no raw food, no alcohol (inferential), (3) Grandma Ruth is on metformin → diabetic → limit sugar (inferential, late-joining entity), (4) Aunt Margaret's celiac is REMOVED (misdiagnosis cleared), (5) Uncle David EXITS early but wants a packed plate (his sodium constraint persists for the plate only, creating scope distinction). At probe time: beef carpaccio=raw→Sarah problem; tiramisu=raw eggs+alcohol→Sarah, sugar→Grandma; honey-glazed ham=high sodium→David's packed plate only; Caesar salad with croutons=fine (Margaret cleared); fruit platter and vegetable skewers=fine for all.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
